answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: A mine operator must immediately contact MSHA within 15 minutes at the toll-free number (1-800-746-1553) once it knows or should know that a death of an individual at the mine has occurred.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes of knowing or should knowing that a death occurred.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust in underground areas of a coal mine must be maintained so that its incombustible content is not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: This 80 percent figure is increased only when methane is present in the ventilating current, implying 80 percent is the baseline requirement with no methane.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be able to protect each underground coal miner for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: Each operator shall make available to each miner who goes underground, and to visitors authorized to enter the mine by the operator, an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold evacuation drills at least once every six months (semi-annually), per 30 CFR 57.4361. Each drill must be held for every shift (at a time other than shift change), involve activation of the fire alarm system, and include evacuation of all persons from their work areas to the surface or designated central evacuation points.

claims.text: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

claims.text: Drills must be held for each shift at a time other than shift change, involve all persons underground, activation of the fire alarm system, and evacuation to the surface or central evacuation points.
claims.quote: The evacuation drills shall—(1) Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground; (2) Involve activation of the fire alarm system; and (3) Include evacuation of all persons from their work areas to the surface or to designated central evacuation points.

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training before such miner is assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The noise standard's permissible exposure level is based on a 90-decibel (dB) criterion level computed as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA8), using a 5-dB exchange rate. Under 30 CFR 62.110, a miner's noise dose must be determined "Use a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate," and dose readings are converted to TWA8 values. The mine operator must ensure no miner's exposure during a work shift exceeds this permissible exposure level (62.130), and in no case may exposure exceed 115 dBA at any time, without adjustment for hearing protectors.

claims.text: The noise dose determination must use a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate.
claims.quote: Use a 90-dB criterion level and a 5-dB exchange rate; and

claims.text: The mine operator must use Table 62-2 when converting from dose readings to equivalent TWA8 readings.
claims.quote: The mine operator must use Table 62-2 when converting from dose readings to equivalent TWA8 readings.

claims.text: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise that exceeds the permissible exposure level.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed during any work shift to noise that exceeds the permissible exposure level.

claims.text: No miner may be exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, as determined without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector.
claims.quote: The mine operator must assure that no miner is exposed at any time to sound levels exceeding 115 dBA, as determined without adjustment for the use of any hearing protector.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: At metal and nonmetal mines, berms or guardrails on the banks of roadways must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (surface metal/nonmetal mines, 56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway (underground metal/nonmetal mines, 57.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air components in an approved refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.
